blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Umamah (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever loved for Allah alone, whoever showed enmity for Allah alone, whoever gave for Allah alone, and whoever withheld (from giving) for Allah alone, has perfected his Iman.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ﵁ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لأَبِي ذَرٍّ: يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ ﵁ أَيُّ عُرَي اْلإِيمَانِ أَوْثَقُ؟ قَالَ: اللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ قَالَ: اَلْمُوَالَاةُ فيِ اللهِ وَالْحُبُّ فيِ اللهِ وَالْبُغْضُ فيِ اللهِ.
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates: The Prophet ﷺ asked Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA), “O Abu Dharr! Which of the knots of Iman is the firmest?” He replied, “Allah and His Rasul know best.” The Prophet ﷺ answered, “Helping one another for Allah alone, loving (one another) for Allah alone, and hating (one another) for Allah alone!”

blocks.text: Explanation:- Whether one makes friendship with another in this world or cuts off friendship, doing so not for one's own desires but for Allah and in submission to His command is among the most important and firmest branches of Iman.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: طُوبَي لِمَنْ آمَنَ بِي وَرَآنِي مَرَّةً وَطُوبَي لِمَنْ آمَنَ بِي وَلَمْ يَرَنِي سَبْعَ مِرَارٍ.
